questions.stem: A student is given a mixture of salt solution and sand. She wants to obtain pure water from the mixture.

parts.label: a
parts.text: She separates the sand from the salt solution. Which method of separation should she use? A crystallisation B filtration C fractional distillation D simple distillation

parts.label: b
parts.text: The student then uses this apparatus to obtain pure water from the salt solution.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Name the pieces of apparatus labelled X, Y and Z.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: State what remains in the flask when the separation is complete.

questions.stem: In a chromatography experiment a student uses samples of three pure food dyes blue (B), red (R) and yellow (Y). He also uses samples of four unknown substances, S, T, U and V. The student puts a small drop of each substance on the pencil line. The diagram shows the student's chromatogram at the end of the experiment.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which of the unknown substances contains only one food dye? A substance S B substance T C substance U D substance V

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain which pure food dyes are in substance V.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the $ R_{f} $ value of the yellow food dye Y. $R _ {\mathrm {f}} =$

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: State how the chromatogram suggests that the yellow food dye Y is less soluble in the solvent than the red food dye R.

questions.stem: A student is provided with a bottle containing a colourless solution X. Solution X is thought to be dilute sulfuric acid of concentration 0.10 mol/dm $ ^{3}. $ The student does some experiments on samples of solution X to try to show that it is dilute sulfuric acid. The student adds a few drops of litmus to a sample of solution X. The litmus turns red.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The student knows that the products of the electrolysis of dilute sulfuric acid are hydrogen and oxygen. She carries out the electrolysis using this apparatus.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Suggest why the student does not use zinc electrodes in her experiment.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: State what is observed at both the anode and the cathode during the electrolysis.

parts.label: a-iii
parts.text: Which of these tests shows that the gas formed at the cathode is hydrogen? A a glowing splint relights B a burning splint gives a squeaky pop C a burning splint goes out D limewater turns cloudy

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe a test to show that solution X contains sulfate ions.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The student then does a titration to see if the concentration of the dilute sulfuric acid is $ 0. 1 0 \mathrm{m o l} / \mathrm{d m}^{3}. $ She measures $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of potassium hydroxide solution into a conical flask, and then adds a few drops of indicator solution.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Name the piece of apparatus the student should use to measure $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of the potassium hydroxide solution.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: The concentration of potassium hydroxide in the solution is $ 0.125 \mathrm{~m o l} / \mathrm{d m}^{3}. $ Calculate the amount, in mol, of KOH in $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of this solution. $\mathrm {a m o u n t} =$

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: The equation for the reaction in the titration is $\mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} + 2 \mathrm {K O H} \rightarrow \mathrm {K} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} + 2 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$ Calculate the volume, in $ cm^{3} $ , of 0.10 mol/dm $ ^{3} $ sulfuric acid needed to neutralise $ 25.0\mathrm{cm}^{3} $ of the potassium hydroxide solution.
